title: Nager.Date public holidays API (country IT, per year)
summary: Public REST API returning the national public-holiday list for a given year and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Probed for IT (national level only) for years 2023, 2024 and 2026, each returning HTTP 200 with JSON records of one holiday per date (date, local and English name, global flag, counties, types). It covers national holidays only, at daily grain, and has no regional or patron-saint holidays for the shop's town. Suitable as the holiday calendar for N4, subject to checking the full list against the official national calendar.

GitHub README (probe_url): 'Easily access public holidays for 200+ countries via .NET, REST API, Docker, or NuGet'; README also shows 'curl http://localhost/api/v4/Holidays/US/2026', i.e. a v4 API exists while the register lists v3.
quality_notes: Endpoint version mismatch: register lists /api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country} and that path responded (HTTP 200). The README documents /api/v4/Holidays/... as the current REST API. Record both; v3 may be deprecated, not verified.

Holiday count per year is 13 for 2023 and 2024 and 14 for 2026 (from the probe 'n_dates' and 'total' fields). The Italian national calendar is commonly listed as about 12 dates; the extra entries were not visible because the probe truncated the list, so the full IT list was not checked against the official calendar. Unverified.
Only the first three records of each year were visible in the probe. Dates of Easter Monday and other moveable holidays were not individually checked.
No regional or local holidays (e.g. patron-saint day of the shop's town) are returned; these need a separate source (N5 or a local calendar).
Sample date range: 2023 and 2024 ranges run 01-01 to 12-26 in the probe; coverage for the window 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31 is confirmed for 2023, 2024 and 2026 only; 2025 was not probed.
No change log, last-updated date or refresh cadence was found; the data is a calendar and is expected to be stable, but this is not documented.
The data licence is not stated separately from the software MIT licence; commercial use of the holiday data itself is therefore unconfirmed.
